claims.claim: In crustaceans, molluscs and oviparous fishes the egg continues to grow after it has been laid.
claims.quote: This same phenomenon is observable in molluscs also, and in such fishes as are oviparous; for in all these cases the egg continues to grow.
measurable_quantities: egg diameter or volume over incubation
claims.candidate_data: Egg-size change during incubation in crustacean, cephalopod and fish embryology studies.

claims.label: Squid, cuttlefish and octopus rarely live beyond a year
claims.claim: The squid and the cuttlefish are short-lived and with few exceptions do not live out a year, and the same is true of the octopus.
claims.quote: The calamary and the cuttle-fish are short-lived, as, with few exceptions, they never see the year out; and the same statement is applicable to the octopus.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of Loligo, Sepia and Octopus species
claims.candidate_data: Cephalopod age (statolith) studies and lifespan records in AnAge and SeaLifeBase.

claims.label: The whole insect grub develops into the animal, not part of it
claims.claim: All insects produce grubs (except one kind of butterfly that lays a hard egg), and the young insect develops from the whole grub, not from a part of it as an animal develops from part of an egg.
claims.quote: But from the grub, the young animal does not grow out of a mere portion of it, as a young animal grows from a portion only of an egg, but the grub entire grows and the animal becomes differentiated out of it.
measurable_quantities: whether insect larvae are wholly transformed into the adult or contain a separate yolk-fed embryo
claims.candidate_data: Insect developmental biology on metamorphosis and egg stages.

claims.label: Intestinal worms do not reproduce their kind
claims.claim: Intestinal worms, of which there are three kinds (flat-worm, round-worm and ascarid), never propagate their kind, although the flat-worm lays something like a melon seed.
claims.quote: These intestinal worms do not in any case propagate their kind.
claims.scope: intestinal worms of man: tapeworm, roundworm, pinworm
measurable_quantities: egg production and life cycles of Taenia, Ascaris and Enterobius
claims.candidate_data: Parasite life-cycle data from CDC DPDx and parasitology literature.

claims.label: Caterpillars feed and excrete; chrysalises do neither
claims.claim: The butterfly caterpillar feeds and voids excrement, but once it becomes a chrysalis it neither feeds nor voids excrement; the same holds for all insects that develop from a grub, such as bees and wasps.
claims.quote: At first, when it is a caterpillar, it feeds and ejects excrement; but when it turns into the chrysalis it neither feeds nor ejects excrement.
measurable_quantities: feeding and excretion during larval vs pupal stages
claims.candidate_data: Insect physiology of the pupal stage; species accounts in the Animal Diversity Web.

claims.label: Generation of grubs is due primarily to the sun's heat or wind
claims.claim: In all grubs and all animals that emerge from the grub state, generation is caused primarily by the heat of the sun or by wind.
claims.quote: With all grubs and all animals that break out from the grub state, generation is due primarily to the heat of the sun or to wind.
measurable_quantities: dependence of insect emergence on temperature
whether larvae arise without eggs
claims.candidate_data: Insect phenology and degree-day development models; spontaneous-generation exclusion experiments.

claims.label: A winged animal in Cyprus is generated in copper-smelting fires
claims.claim: In Cyprus, where copper ore is smelted, a winged animal somewhat larger than a bluebottle fly is generated in the fire, can hop or crawl through it, and perishes when kept away from the fire.
claims.quote: In Cyprus, in places where copper-ore is smelted, with heaps of the ore piled on day after day, an animal is engendered in the fire, somewhat larger than a blue bottle fly, furnished with wings, which can hop or crawl through the fire.
claims.scope: an unnamed insect of Cypriot copper smelters
measurable_quantities: survival of any insect in smelting fires
claims.candidate_data: Upper thermal limits of insects in thermal-tolerance compilations such as GlobTherm.

claims.label: Ichneumon wasps provision mud-sealed holes with dead spiders
claims.claim: The wasps called ichneumons, smaller than ordinary wasps, kill spiders, carry them to a hole in a wall, seal it with mud and lay their grubs inside, and from the grubs come new ichneumons.
claims.quote: kill spiders and carry off the dead bodies to a wall or some such place with a hole in it; this hole they smear over with mud and lay their grubs inside it, and from the grubs come the hunter-wasps
measurable_quantities: prey type and nest construction of spider-hunting wasps
claims.candidate_data: Nesting-biology accounts for Pompilidae and Sceliphron in the entomological literature and the Animal Diversity Web.

claims.label: Bees make wax from flowers but gather honey from the air
claims.claim: The bee makes wax from flowers but does not make honey; it merely gathers honey that is deposited out of the atmosphere as dew.
claims.quote: The bee, then, makes the wax from flowers. The honey, however, it does not make, but merely gathers what is deposited out of the atmosphere
measurable_quantities: origin of honey sugars (floral nectar or honeydew vs atmospheric dew)
glandular origin of wax
claims.candidate_data: Apicultural physiology on nectar processing and wax glands; melissopalynology of honey.

claims.label: A bee lives six years, at most seven
claims.claim: The bee lives six years as a rule and seven at most.
claims.quote: The bee lives for six years as a rule, as an exception for seven years.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of worker and queen honey bees
colony longevity
claims.candidate_data: Honey bee longevity records in AnAge and apicultural literature.

claims.label: Young scorpions and spiders kill their parent after hatching
claims.claim: When the land-scorpion's brood has hatched, the young eject and kill the parent, as also happens with the spider.
claims.quote: When the hatching is completed, the parent animal, as happens with the parent spider, is ejected and put to death by the young ones
measurable_quantities: incidence of matriphagy in scorpions and spiders
claims.candidate_data: Arachnological studies of matriphagy and maternal care.

claims.label: Grasshoppers lay eggs at summer's end and then die
claims.claim: The grasshopper lays its eggs at the close of summer and dies after laying them, the males dying about the same time.
claims.quote: The grasshopper lays its eggs at the close of summer, and dies after laying them.
measurable_quantities: adult lifespan after oviposition and oviposition season in grasshoppers
claims.candidate_data: Life-history records for Orthoptera in the Orthoptera Species File and entomological literature.

claims.label: Only male cicadas sing
claims.claim: In both the large and small cicadas it is the male that sings and the female is silent.
claims.quote: In both species, the larger and the smaller, it is the male that sings, and the female that is unvocal.
measurable_quantities: presence of tymbal sound organs by sex in cicadas
claims.candidate_data: Cicada acoustic anatomy and bioacoustic recordings in the entomological literature.

claims.label: Lice, fleas and bugs produce nits that generate nothing
claims.claim: Insects that live on the juices of living flesh, such as lice, fleas and bugs, all produce nits, and these nits produce nothing further.
claims.quote: all, without exception, generate what are called 'nits', and these nits generate nothing
measurable_quantities: hatching of louse, flea and bedbug eggs into nymphs or larvae
claims.candidate_data: Life cycles of Pediculus, Pulex and Cimex in medical entomology references such as CDC DPDx.

claims.label: The ass alone among hairy animals has neither lice nor ticks
claims.claim: All feathered and hair-coated animals are infested with lice, with the single exception of the ass, which has neither lice nor ticks.
claims.quote: All other winged animals that are furnished with feathers are similarly infested, and all hair-coated creatures also, with the single exception of the ass, which is infested neither with lice nor with ticks.
measurable_quantities: records of lice and ticks on donkeys
louse presence across bird and mammal hosts
claims.candidate_data: Host-parasite association records for Haematopinus asini and ticks on Equus asinus in veterinary parasitology databases.

claims.label: Fig-wasps from wild figs enter cultivated figs and keep them from dropping
claims.claim: The fig-wasp develops in the fruit of the wild fig, then flies into the fruit of the cultivated fig through its opening and makes the fruit stay on the tree, which is why farmers hang wild figs on fig trees.
claims.quote: the psen leaves the husk behind it and flies away, and enters into the fruit of the fig-tree through its orifice, and causes the fruit not to drop off
claims.scope: fig wasp (Blastophaga psenes) and Ficus carica (caprification)
measurable_quantities: fruit retention of caprified vs uncaprified figs
claims.candidate_data: Horticultural studies of caprification in Smyrna-type figs and fig-wasp pollination ecology.

claims.label: The viper is internally oviparous and externally viviparous
claims.claim: The viper produces eggs internally but gives birth to live young, all in one day, about twenty in number and one at a time, whereas other serpents lay eggs.
claims.quote: the viper is externally viviparous, having been previously oviparous internally
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode and litter size of Vipera species
claims.candidate_data: Reproductive mode and clutch or litter size in the Reptile Database and the Amniote Life-History Database.

claims.label: Birds of prey lay few eggs, the kestrel excepted
claims.claim: All birds of prey (birds with crooked talons) are unprolific, except the kestrel, which is the most prolific of them and lays four or occasionally more eggs.
claims.quote: All birds of prey, or birds with crooked talons, are unprolific, except the kestrel: this bird is the most prolific of birds of prey; as many as four eggs have been observed in the nest, and occasionally it lays even more.
measurable_quantities: clutch size across raptor species
kestrel clutch size relative to other raptors
claims.candidate_data: Clutch-size compilations in the Amniote Life-History Database and Birds of the World.

claims.label: Waterbird eggs have more yolk and less white than landbird eggs
claims.claim: The eggs of birds that frequent rivers and marshes have proportionally more yolk and less white than the eggs of land birds.
claims.quote: the eggs of waterbirds have comparatively more of the yellow or yolk and less of the white
claims.scope: waterbirds (marsh and river birds) versus land birds
measurable_quantities: yolk mass as a fraction of egg mass across species
habitat of each species
claims.candidate_data: Published comparative egg-composition data (yolk fraction by species and developmental mode); habitat traits in AVONET.

claims.label: Long pointed eggs hatch females, rounded eggs hatch males
claims.claim: Long, pointed eggs produce females, while round eggs, or eggs more rounded at the narrow end, produce males.
claims.quote: Long and pointed eggs are female; those that are round, or more rounded at the narrow end, are male.
measurable_quantities: egg shape index
sex of the hatched chick
claims.candidate_data: Poultry studies relating egg shape index to embryo sex.

claims.label: Hens and geese lay wind-eggs without ever copulating
claims.claim: Wind-eggs (infertile eggs) are not residues of earlier copulation: hens and geese that have never copulated lay them.
claims.quote: we have cases well authenticated where chickens of the common hen and goose have laid wind-eggs without ever having been subjected to copulation
claims.scope: domestic hen, goose; also partridge, pigeon, peahen, vulpanser
measurable_quantities: laying by females kept isolated from males
claims.candidate_data: Poultry husbandry records of egg production by unmated flocks.

claims.label: Egg and incubation periods in birds increase with body size
claims.claim: The time for an egg to form after copulation and for the chick to hatch differs between birds according to the size of the parents.
claims.quote: The generation of the egg after copulation and the generation of the chick from the subsequent hatching of the egg are not brought about within equal periods for all birds, but differ as to time according to the size of the parent-birds.
measurable_quantities: incubation period
adult body mass
claims.candidate_data: Incubation period and body mass in the Amniote Life-History Database and AVONET.

claims.label: The heart is the first organ, a beating speck of blood
claims.claim: The heart appears in the developing egg as a speck of blood that beats and moves as though alive, and two blood vessels lead from it.
claims.quote: and the heart appears, like a speck of blood, in the white of the egg. This point beats and moves as though endowed with life, and from it two vein-ducts with blood in them trend in a convoluted course
measurable_quantities: order of organ appearance
onset of heartbeat
claims.candidate_data: Chick embryo staging (Hamburger–Hamilton) and developmental anatomy in Uberon.

claims.label: The chick forms from the white and is nourished by the yolk
claims.claim: The principle of life of the chick lies in the white of the egg, while its nutriment comes from the yolk through a navel-string.
claims.quote: The life-element of the chick is in the white of the egg, and the nutriment comes through the navel-string out of the yolk.
measurable_quantities: embryo origin relative to yolk and albumen
contribution of yolk and albumen to embryo nutrition
claims.candidate_data: Avian embryology literature on the blastoderm, yolk sac and albumen uptake.

claims.label: Very few birds breed in their first year
claims.claim: Very few birds breed within their first year.
claims.quote: Very few birds propagate within their first year.
measurable_quantities: age at first breeding across bird species
claims.candidate_data: Age at maturity in AnAge and the Amniote Life-History Database.

claims.label: Blinded swallow chicks recover their sight
claims.claim: If the eyes of young swallow chicks are pricked out, the birds recover and later see again.
claims.quote: If you prick out the eyes of swallow chicks while they are yet young, the birds will get well again and will see by and by.
measurable_quantities: recovery of vision after eye injury in nestlings
claims.candidate_data: Avian retinal and corneal regeneration literature; none known for this exact procedure.

claims.label: The eagle usually rears two young and expels one from the nest
claims.claim: The eagle usually lays three eggs and hatches two (occasionally three), and as the young grow the mother, wearied of feeding them, expels one from the nest; she broods for about thirty days.
claims.quote: This is the case in most instances, though occasionally a brood of three has been observed. As the young ones grow, the mother becomes wearied with feeding them and extrudes one of the pair from the nest.
measurable_quantities: clutch size
brood size at fledging
brood reduction by siblicide or parental ejection
claims.candidate_data: Breeding studies of Aquila eagles recording clutch size, siblicide and fledging success; Birds of the World.

claims.label: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk
claims.claim: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk: it lacks the hawk's crooked talons, resembles the pigeon in head and claws, and is preyed on by hawks, which never happens between birds of one kind.
claims.quote: The cuckoo has been seen to be preyed on by the hawk; and this never happens between birds of the same species.
measurable_quantities: predation of cuckoos by hawks
phylogenetic placement of cuckoos versus hawks
claims.candidate_data: Open Tree of Life for the relationship of Cuculidae and Accipitridae; diet records of Accipiter in Birds of the World.

claims.label: The cuckoo builds no nest and lays in other birds' nests
claims.claim: The cuckoo builds no nest but lays its egg, usually one, in the nest of a smaller bird, after devouring that bird's eggs, and the host bird hatches and rears the young cuckoo.
claims.quote: The bird eggs, but does not build a nest. Sometimes it lays its eggs in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring the eggs of this bird
claims.scope: common cuckoo (Cuculus canorus); hosts include the hypolais
measurable_quantities: brood parasitism
removal of host eggs by the laying female
host species and body size
claims.candidate_data: Brood-parasitism and host-use records for Cuculus canorus in Birds of the World and published host databases.

claims.label: Bird testes enlarge in the breeding season, most in salacious birds
claims.claim: In male birds the testicles are visibly larger at pairing time than at other times, most conspicuously in the more salacious birds such as the cock and the cock partridge.
claims.quote: With male birds about pairing time the testicles are obviously larger than at other times, and this is conspicuously the case with the more salacious birds, such as the barn-door cock and the cock partridge
measurable_quantities: seasonal change in testis mass
relative testis mass against mating frequency
claims.candidate_data: Comparative datasets of avian testis mass and seasonal gonadal recrudescence.

claims.label: Cartilaginous fishes are viviparous after internal eggs
claims.claim: Cartilaginous fishes (selachians) are viviparous and all other fishes are oviparous; selachians first produce eggs internally and then bear live young, the fishing-frog excepted.
claims.quote: Fishes of the cartilaginous genus are viviparous; the rest are oviparous. And cartilaginous fishes are first oviparous internally and subsequently viviparous; they rear the embryos internally, the batrachus or fishing-frog being an exception.
claims.scope: selachians (sharks and rays) versus other fishes; fishing-frog (Lophius)
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparous, yolk-sac viviparous, placental) across fish taxa
claims.candidate_data: Reproductive mode fields in FishBase.

claims.label: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a cord attached to the womb
claims.claim: In the smooth shark the young develop with a navel-string attached to the womb, so that once the yolk is used up the embryo is sustained as in quadrupeds, with a chorion and membranes.
claims.quote: the young develop with the navel-string attached to the womb, so that, as the egg-substance gets used up, the embryo is sustained to all appearance just as in the case of quadrupeds
measurable_quantities: presence of a yolk-sac placenta
maternal nutrient transfer to embryos
claims.candidate_data: Reproductive mode records in FishBase; histological studies of the Mustelus yolk-sac placenta.

claims.label: Selachians come inshore to give birth, for warmth and protection
claims.claim: Cartilaginous fishes move from the open and deep sea towards the shore to bear their young, for the sake of warmth and of protection for the young.
claims.quote: Cartilaginous fishes come out from the main seas and deep waters towards the shore and there bring forth their young, and they do so for the sake of warmth and by way of protection for their young.
measurable_quantities: depth and distance from shore of pupping and nursery areas
neonate predation risk inshore versus offshore
claims.candidate_data: Shark nursery-area studies; depth distributions of neonates in GBIF and OBIS occurrence data.

claims.label: Fishes of different kinds do not interbreed
claims.claim: As a general rule no kind of fish pairs with another kind.
claims.quote: Observations would lead to the general rule that no one variety of fish pairs with another variety.
measurable_quantities: frequency of interspecific hybridization in wild fishes
claims.candidate_data: Published reviews and genetic surveys of natural hybridization in fishes.

claims.label: All cetaceans are viviparous, never carrying eggs
claims.claim: The dolphin, the whale and all other cetaceans (animals with a blow-hole instead of gills) are viviparous, carrying an embryo rather than eggs, as do humans and viviparous quadrupeds.
claims.quote: The dolphin, the whale, and all the rest of the Cetacea, all, that is to say, that are provided with a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous.
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode in Cetacea
claims.candidate_data: Cetacean life-history accounts in the Animal Diversity Web and PanTHERIA.

claims.label: Dolphins and porpoises suckle their young
claims.claim: The dolphin and the porpoise have milk and suckle their young.
claims.quote: The dolphin and the porpoise are provided with milk, and suckle their young.
measurable_quantities: lactation in Delphinidae and Phocoenidae
claims.candidate_data: Lactation duration in PanTHERIA and the Animal Diversity Web.

claims.label: All scaly fishes are oviparous
claims.claim: All scaly fishes are oviparous, as are all smooth or slippery fishes except the eel.
claims.quote: all scaly fish are oviparous, as the basse, the mullet, the grey mullet, and the etelis, and all the so-called white-fish, and all the smooth or slippery fish except the eel
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode across scaled bony fishes
claims.candidate_data: Reproductive mode fields in FishBase (live-bearing teleosts such as Poeciliidae, Zoarces, Sebastes).

claims.label: Erythrinus and channa are always caught full of eggs
claims.claim: Fishes are mostly divided into males and females, but specimens of the erythrinus and the channa are never caught except full of eggs.
claims.quote: Fishes for the most part are divided into males and females, but one is puzzled to account for the erythrinus and the channa, for specimens of these species are never caught except in a condition of pregnancy.
claims.scope: channa (likely Serranus cabrilla) and erythrinus (a sea bream or serranid)
measurable_quantities: presence of males
simultaneous hermaphroditism
claims.candidate_data: Sexual system data for Serranus in FishBase and the fish hermaphroditism literature.

claims.label: Only fish eggs sprinkled with milt after laying develop
claims.claim: In oviparous fishes the female lays her eggs and the male then sheds milt over them; only the eggs so sprinkled produce young, the rest being lost.
claims.quote: The greater number of these eggs so deposited are not productive, but only those over which the male sheds the milt or sperm; for when the female has laid her eggs, the male follows and sheds its sperm over them
measurable_quantities: fertilization rate with and without milt
claims.candidate_data: Fish fertilization biology and hatchery data; fertilization mode in FishBase.

claims.label: Fishes spawn inshore for warmth, food and protection from predators
claims.claim: Fishes in general lay their eggs close to shore, because inshore water is warmer, richer in food, and protects the spawn from larger fishes.
claims.quote: for the water close in to shore is warm and is better supplied with food than the outer sea, and serves as a protection to the spawn against the voracity of the larger fish
measurable_quantities: spawning depth and distance from shore
egg predation rates inshore versus offshore
claims.candidate_data: Spawning-ground data in FishBase; ichthyoplankton surveys.

claims.label: In fish embryos the large eyes are the first organs visible
claims.claim: In oviparous fishes the embryo forms at the upper end of the egg within a membrane and its large spherical eyes are the first organs visible, so fishes do not develop like grubs, which form the lower end first.
claims.quote: the embryo comes at the upper end of the egg and is enveloped in a membrane, and the eyes, large and spherical, are the first organs visible
measurable_quantities: order of organ appearance in fish embryos
claims.candidate_data: Zebrafish and other teleost embryonic staging series (e.g. ZFIN staging).

claims.label: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
claims.claim: In the sheat-fish the eggs develop exceptionally slowly and the male guards the spawn for forty or fifty days against small fishes, while the female leaves after spawning.
claims.quote: In the case of the sheat-fish the growth from the egg is exceptionally slow, and, in consequence, the male has to keep watch for forty or fifty days to prevent the-spawn being devoured by such little fishes as chance to come by.
measurable_quantities: sex of guarding parent
duration of egg and fry guarding
egg development time
claims.candidate_data: FishBase species account and field studies of Silurus aristotelis paternal care.

claims.label: Eels go down from rivers to the sea while mullet go up
claims.claim: The mullet migrates up from the sea into marshes and rivers, while eels migrate down from marshes and rivers to the sea.
claims.quote: The mullet goes up from the sea to marshes and rivers; the eels, on the contrary, make their way down from the marshes and rivers to the sea.
measurable_quantities: direction and timing of migration between fresh water and sea
claims.candidate_data: Migration type (catadromous, amphidromous) in FishBase; eel silver-eel migration studies.

claims.label: Some fishes arise spontaneously from mud and sand
claims.claim: Certain fishes come into existence spontaneously, not from eggs or copulation, arising from mud or from sand and decaying matter; such fry cannot grow or reproduce.
claims.quote: From the facts above enumerated it is quite proved that certain fishes come spontaneously into existence, not being derived from eggs or from copulation.
claims.scope: small fry (aphya) in ponds and sandy shallows; a kind of mullet near Cnidos
measurable_quantities: origin of fish appearing in refilled ponds (eggs, aestivation, immigration)
claims.candidate_data: Studies of annual killifish and egg-bank survival in ephemeral pools; biogenesis experiments.

claims.label: Eels have no milt, spawn or reproductive passages
claims.claim: Eels are neither born from pairing nor oviparous: no eel has ever been found with milt or spawn, nor with passages for spawn or eggs.
claims.quote: nor was an eel ever found supplied with either milt or spawn, nor are they when cut open found to have within them passages for spawn or for eggs
measurable_quantities: gonad presence and development in yellow and silver eels
claims.candidate_data: Anguilla gonad histology studies; FishBase species account.

claims.label: Eels arise from 'earth's guts' in mud and wet ground
claims.claim: Eels arise from the so-called 'earth's guts', worms that grow spontaneously in mud and humid ground where sun heat causes putrefaction.
claims.quote: Eels are derived from the so-called 'earth's guts' that grow spontaneously in mud and in humid ground
measurable_quantities: origin of glass eels and elvers
claims.candidate_data: Eel life-cycle studies (Sargasso Sea spawning, leptocephalus larvae); FishBase.

claims.label: Fish gestation always lasts a number of days divisible by seven
claims.claim: In fishes gestation lasts thirty days or less, but always a number of days divisible by seven.
claims.quote: With some fishes the time of gestation is not longer than thirty days, with others it is a lesser period; but with all it extends over a number of days divisible by seven.
measurable_quantities: duration of egg-carrying or incubation in days
claims.candidate_data: Incubation and gestation durations in FishBase.

claims.label: Viviparous selachians are less fecund but their young survive better
claims.claim: Cartilaginous fishes as a rule are less prolific than other fishes because they are viviparous, and their young, being large, have a better chance of escaping destruction.
claims.quote: As a rule, cartilaginous fish are less prolific than other fish owing to their being viviparous; and their young by reason of their size have a better chance of escaping destruction.
measurable_quantities: fecundity
offspring size
early survival
claims.candidate_data: Fecundity, size at birth and reproductive mode in FishBase.

claims.label: Females are fiercest after giving birth, males in the rut
claims.claim: Female animals are most bad-tempered just after giving birth and males during the pairing season.
claims.quote: The female is most cross-tempered just after parturition, the male during the time of pairing
claims.scope: viviparous land animals: horse, boar, bull, ram, camel, bear, wolf, lion, dog
measurable_quantities: aggression rates by sex and reproductive stage
claims.candidate_data: Behavioural studies of maternal aggression and male rut aggression in mammals.

claims.label: Breeding seasons are timed so the young are reared at a good season
claims.claim: Sexual appetite is keenest in spring, but the pairing season differs between animals and is adapted so that the young are reared at a convenient season.
claims.quote: In general the sexual appetites of animals are keenest in spring-time; the time of pairing, however, is not the same for all, but is adapted so as to ensure the rearing of the young at a convenient season.
measurable_quantities: mating month
gestation length
birth month relative to food peak
claims.candidate_data: Mating season and gestation length in PanTHERIA and AnAge.

claims.label: North winds at mating give male lambs, south winds female
claims.claim: Sheep and goats mated when north winds blow tend to bear males, and when south winds blow, females.
claims.quote: And if they submit to the male when north winds are blowing, they are apt to bear males; if when south winds are blowing, females.
measurable_quantities: offspring sex ratio against wind direction at mating
claims.candidate_data: Flock breeding records joined to historical wind data.

claims.label: Male horses die sooner because of the cost of sexual service
claims.claim: The male horse is shorter-lived than the female because of the sexual service it renders, and stable-reared horses live longer than those reared in troops.
claims.quote: The male is less long-lived than the female by reason of the sexual service he is called on to render; and horses that are reared in a private stable live longer than such as are reared in troops.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of breeding stallions, geldings and mares
lifespan by husbandry
claims.candidate_data: Equine longevity studies by sex, castration and use.

claims.label: Hybrid gestation follows the sire; the foal resembles the mother
claims.claim: In a cross between horse and ass, gestation lasts as long as it would for the sire's own species, while in size, looks and vigour the foal tends to resemble the mother more than the sire.
claims.quote: The period for gestation in the case of a cross depends on the male, and is just what it would have been if the male had had commerce with a female of his own kind. In regard to size, looks, and vigour, the foal is more apt to resemble the mother than the sire.
measurable_quantities: gestation length of mules and hinnies against parental species
size of mules versus hinnies
claims.candidate_data: Equine hybrid gestation and body-size studies.

claims.label: Female mules can conceive but never carry to birth
claims.claim: A female mule has been known to be impregnated, but without giving birth.
claims.quote: A female mule has been known to be impregnated, but without the impregnation being followed up by parturition.
measurable_quantities: conception and live-birth rates in female mules
claims.candidate_data: Veterinary case reports of fertile mules and equine hybrid cytogenetics.

claims.label: Short gestation and fast growth argue against long deer lifespans
claims.claim: The short gestation and rapid growth of the fawn indicate that the deer is not extremely long-lived, contrary to fabulous stories.
claims.quote: the brevity of the period of gestation and the rapidity of growth in the fawn would not lead one to attribute extreme longevity to this creature
measurable_quantities: gestation length
postnatal growth rate
maximum lifespan
claims.candidate_data: Gestation, growth and maximum longevity across mammals in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

claims.label: Bear cubs are the smallest newborns relative to the mother
claims.claim: Of all animals the newborn bear cub is the smallest relative to its mother, larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel, and is born hairless, blind and with its limbs and organs unformed.
claims.quote: Of all animals the newly born cub of the she bear is the smallest in proportion to the size of the mother; that is to say, it is larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel.
measurable_quantities: neonate mass as a fraction of maternal mass across mammals
claims.candidate_data: Neonate and adult body mass in PanTHERIA and the Amniote Life-History Database.

claims.label: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites
claims.claim: It is untrue that every hyena has the organs of both sexes: the male has a male organ like the dog's and a blind female-like part under the tail, and the female has a blind male-like part and a true female organ.
claims.quote: What is recounted concerning its genital organs, to the effect that every hyena is furnished with the organ both of the male and the female, is untrue.
measurable_quantities: external genital anatomy by sex
claims.candidate_data: Comparative anatomy of hyaenid genitalia (subcaudal scent pouch in striped hyena); the Animal Diversity Web.

claims.label: Hares breed year-round, superfoetate and bear every month
claims.claim: Hares breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, bear young every month, and can conceive again immediately after giving birth while suckling.
claims.quote: They breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, and bear young every month.
measurable_quantities: superfetation
breeding season length
litters per year
claims.candidate_data: Reproductive studies of superfetation in Lepus europaeus; litters per year in PanTHERIA.

claims.label: Mice are the most prolific animals in litter size and frequency
claims.claim: The mouse is the most astonishing of animals in generation, both for the number of its young and for how quickly births recur.
claims.quote: The phenomena of generation in regard to the mouse are the most astonishing both for the number of the young and for the rapidity of recurrence in the births.
measurable_quantities: litter size
interbirth interval
annual reproductive output relative to other mammals
claims.candidate_data: Litter size and litters per year in PanTHERIA and AnAge.

claims.label: Male puberty begins at about fourteen with seed and pubic hair
claims.claim: In most cases a boy begins to produce seed at about fourteen years of age, and pubic hair appears at the same time.
claims.quote: When twice seven years old, in the most of cases, the male begins to engender seed; and at the same time hair appears upon the pubes
measurable_quantities: age at spermarche
age at onset of pubic hair (Tanner stage 2)
claims.candidate_data: Pubertal timing cohorts and surveys such as NHANES and longitudinal growth studies reporting age at spermarche and pubic hair stages.

claims.label: Menstruation and breast growth begin at about fourteen in girls
claims.claim: In girls, at about fourteen years of age (the same age as male puberty), the breasts swell and menstruation begins.
claims.quote: At the same age in the female, the breasts swell and the so-called catamenia commence to flow
measurable_quantities: age at menarche
age at thelarche
claims.candidate_data: Age-at-menarche data from NHANES, the Demographic and Health Surveys and historical menarche series.

claims.label: Semen is infertile until twenty-one and young parents have small, imperfect offspring
claims.claim: Until about the age of twenty-one a man's seed is infertile; after that it becomes fertile, but very young men and women produce undersized and imperfect offspring, as do young animals generally.
claims.quote: At the outset and till the age of one and twenty the spermatic discharge is devoid of fecundity; afterwards it becomes fertile, but young men and women produce undersized and imperfect progeny, as is the case also with the common run of animals.
claims.scope: humans, and animals generally for the effect of parental youth
measurable_quantities: male fertility by age under 21
birth weight and congenital anomaly rates by maternal and paternal age
claims.candidate_data: National birth registries and vital statistics giving birth weight and anomalies by parental age; the Human Fertility Database for age-specific fertility.

claims.label: Thick, granular semen tends to produce males and thin semen females
claims.claim: Thin seed is infertile; granular seed is fertile and likely to produce male children, while thin, unclotted seed tends to produce female children.
claims.quote: When the spermatic fluid is of a thin consistency it is infertile; when granular it is fertile and likely to produce male children, but when thin and unclotted it is apt to produce female offspring.
measurable_quantities: semen viscosity or consistency
fertility outcome
offspring sex ratio by semen consistency
claims.candidate_data: Clinical semen-analysis datasets linked to IVF and pregnancy outcomes, including offspring sex; none known as a public standard resource.

claims.label: In non-viviparous animals the menstrual residue becomes body, scales and feathers
claims.claim: Animals that do not bear live young have no menstrual discharge, because the corresponding residue is turned into bodily substance, scutes, scales or feathers; in viviparous quadrupeds it becomes hair, flesh and urine, and only in women is it discharged.
claims.quote: In creatures that do not bring forth their young alive nothing of the sort manifests itself, this particular superfluity being converted into bodily substance
claims.scope: all animals; oviparous animals (birds, reptiles, fishes) contrasted with viviparous quadrupeds and women
measurable_quantities: presence or absence of menstruation across taxa
claims.candidate_data: Comparative reproductive physiology surveys of menstruation across mammals; the Animal Diversity Web for reproductive traits.

claims.label: A male foetus first moves at about forty days, a female at about ninety
claims.claim: A male foetus usually first moves on the right side of the womb at about the fortieth day, a female on the left side at about the ninetieth day, though there are many exceptions.
claims.quote: In the case of male children the first movement usually occurs on the right-hand side of the womb and about the fortieth day, but if the child be a female then on the left-hand side and about the ninetieth day.
measurable_quantities: gestational age at first foetal movement by sex
side of first movement by sex
claims.candidate_data: Obstetric ultrasound studies of onset of foetal movement by sex; maternal quickening surveys.

claims.label: An aborted male embryo at forty days is ant-sized with limbs and eyes visible
claims.claim: A male human embryo aborted at the fortieth day is about the size of a large ant, with all the limbs, the penis and the disproportionately large eyes plainly visible.
claims.quote: If the membrane be pulled to bits the embryo is revealed, as big as one of the large kind of ants; and all the limbs are plain to see, including the penis, and the eyes also, which as in other animals are of great size.
claims.scope: human embryos at about forty days
measurable_quantities: crown-rump length at about six weeks
visibility of limbs, eyes and genital tubercle
claims.candidate_data: Embryological staging collections such as the Carnegie stages and the Human Developmental Biology Resource.

claims.label: Female embryos develop more slowly in the womb than male embryos
claims.claim: In the womb a female embryo completes the development of its parts more slowly than a male, and more often than a male takes ten months to reach full term.
claims.quote: In short, while within the womb, the female infant accomplishes the whole development of its parts more slowly than the male, and more frequently than the man-child takes ten months to come to perfection.
measurable_quantities: gestation length by foetal sex
embryonic developmental stage by sex at fixed age
claims.candidate_data: National birth registries giving gestational age by infant sex.

claims.label: Humans alone have a variable term of pregnancy, from seven to eleven months
claims.claim: Every other animal has a single fixed term of pregnancy, but in humans alone it varies, lasting seven, eight, nine or, most commonly, ten months, and occasionally into the eleventh.
claims.quote: But in the case of mankind alone of all animals the times are diverse; for pregnancy may be of seven months' duration, or of eight months or of nine, and still more commonly of ten months, while some few women go even into the eleventh month.
claims.scope: humans compared with all other animals
measurable_quantities: variance of gestation length in humans
variance of gestation length in other mammals
claims.candidate_data: Human birth registries for gestational age; AnAge and the Amniote Life-History Database for gestation lengths in other mammals (variance would need primary studies).

claims.label: Children born before seven months never survive
claims.claim: Children born before the seventh month of pregnancy can never survive; seven-month children are the earliest viable, and most of them are weakly.
claims.quote: Children that come into the world before seven months can under no circumstances survive. The seven-months' children are the earliest that are capable of life, and most of them are weakly
measurable_quantities: survival by gestational age at birth
claims.candidate_data: Neonatal survival-by-gestational-age data from national birth and infant death registries; historical pre-incubator series would be needed for a fair test.

claims.label: Eight-month children mostly die in Greece but survive in Egypt
claims.claim: Children born in the eighth month are reared successfully in Egypt and some other places, but in Greece only a few survive and most perish.
claims.quote: in these places the eight-months' children live and are brought up, but in Greece it is only a few of them that survive while most perish.
claims.scope: human births at about eight months' gestation, Egypt versus Greece
measurable_quantities: survival of eight-month (about 32–36 week) births
survival compared with seven-month births
claims.candidate_data: Neonatal survival by gestational week from modern registries; ancient regional data none known.

claims.label: The most children a woman has borne at one birth is five
claims.claim: The largest number of children ever born to a woman at one birth is five, which has been observed several times.
claims.quote: The largest number ever brought forth is five, and such an occurrence has been witnessed on several occasions.
measurable_quantities: maximum recorded human litter size
frequency of quintuplet births
claims.candidate_data: Multiple-birth records from national vital statistics and medical case reports.

claims.label: Women and mares, unlike other animals, accept the male during pregnancy
claims.claim: Of all animals the woman and the mare are most inclined to accept mating during pregnancy; all other animals avoid the male when pregnant, except those that show superfoetation, such as the hare.
claims.quote: Of all animals the woman and the mare are most inclined to receive the commerce of the male during pregnancy; while all other animals when they are pregnant avoid the male, save those in which the phenomenon of superfoetation occurs, such as the hare.
claims.scope: humans, horses, hares and other animals
measurable_quantities: frequency of mating during pregnancy by species
occurrence of superfoetation in hares
claims.candidate_data: Behavioural studies of mating during gestation in mammals; reproductive studies of superfetation in the European brown hare (Lepus europaeus).

claims.label: Menstruation ceases at about forty, at the latest fifty, ending childbearing
claims.claim: In most women menstruation ceases at about forty; in some it lasts until fifty, and women of that age have borne children, but none beyond it.
claims.quote: the menstrual discharges ceases in most women about their fortieth year; but with those in whom it goes on longer it lasts even to the fiftieth year, and women of that age have been known to bear children. But beyond that age there is no case on record.
measurable_quantities: age at menopause
maximum maternal age at natural conception
claims.candidate_data: Age-at-menopause cohort studies and the Human Fertility Database for age-specific fertility at 40–50+.

claims.label: Men remain fertile to sixty and sometimes seventy
claims.claim: Men in most cases remain sexually competent until sixty, and some until seventy; men have fathered children at seventy.
claims.quote: Men in most cases continue to be sexually competent until they are sixty years old, and if that limit be overpassed then until seventy years; and men have been actually known to procreate children at seventy years of age.
measurable_quantities: age-specific male fertility
maximum paternal age
claims.candidate_data: Paternal-age distributions in national birth registries.

claims.label: Children often inherit their parents' deformities and acquired marks
claims.claim: Deformed parents produce deformed children (lame from lame, blind from blind), and children often inherit their parents' peculiarities, including marks such as pimples or scars.
claims.quote: From deformed parents come deformed children, lame from lame and blind from blind, and, speaking generally, children often inherit anything that is peculiar in their parents and are born with similar marks, such as pimples or scars.
measurable_quantities: recurrence of parental congenital and acquired traits in offspring
claims.candidate_data: Family recurrence data for congenital disorders (e.g. OMIM entries and registry studies); offspring of parents with acquired injuries as a control.

claims.label: Resemblance can skip a generation and reappear in grandchildren
claims.claim: Children usually resemble their parents or ancestors, but resemblance can be passed on after several generations, appearing in a grandchild but not in the child.
claims.quote: While children mostly resemble their parents or their ancestors, it sometimes happens that no such resemblance is to be traced. But parents may pass on resemblance after several generations
measurable_quantities: frequency of traits reappearing in grandchildren but absent in parents
claims.candidate_data: Pedigree data for recessive traits, e.g. OMIM and published family studies.

claims.label: All animals develop in the same way, differing in where the navel attaches
claims.claim: All animals, whether flying, swimming or walking, viviparous or oviparous, develop in the same way, except that in viviparous animals the navel is attached to the womb, in others to the egg, and in certain fishes to both.
claims.quote: All animals whatsoever, whether they fly or swim or walk upon dry land, whether they bring forth their young alive or in the egg, develop in the same way: save only that some have the navel attached to the womb, namely the viviparous animals, and some have it attached to the egg, and some to both parts alike, as in a certain sort of fishes.
claims.scope: all animals; 'a certain sort of fishes' (placental sharks such as the smooth dogfish)
measurable_quantities: umbilical attachment to uterus, yolk or both across taxa
claims.candidate_data: Comparative embryology in the literature and Uberon/Phenoscape annotations of yolk-sac and placental structures.

claims.label: All animals are born head first in the natural course
claims.claim: All animals are at first head-upward in the womb but turn downward near term, and in the natural course birth in all animals is head first.
claims.quote: birth in the natural course of things takes place in all animals head foremost
measurable_quantities: proportion of head-first presentations by species
claims.candidate_data: Veterinary obstetric data on foetal presentation in horses, cattle and sheep; cetacean birth observations (often tail-first).

claims.label: The navel-string has four vessels in oxen, two in smaller animals, one in fowls
claims.claim: The navel-string contains four blood vessels in large animals such as oxen, two in smaller animals, and only one in very small ones such as fowls.
claims.quote: In the larger animals, such as the embryos of oxen, the vessels are four in number, and in smaller animals two; in the very little ones, such as fowls, one vessel only.
measurable_quantities: number of umbilical vessels by species and body size
claims.candidate_data: Comparative embryology and veterinary anatomy texts; Uberon annotations of umbilical artery and vein.

claims.label: Children cut their first teeth in the seventh month, front teeth first
claims.claim: Children begin cutting teeth in the seventh month, the front teeth first, upper or lower; teeth come sooner the warmer the nurse's milk.
claims.quote: children begin to cut their teeth in the seventh month; and the front teeth are the first to come through, sometimes the upper and sometimes the lower ones.
measurable_quantities: age at first tooth eruption
order of eruption
claims.candidate_data: Paediatric tooth-eruption norms from growth cohort studies.

claims.label: Menstruation is suppressed while milk flows
claims.claim: As a general rule menstruation does not occur while a woman is producing milk, because moisture is not directed in several directions at once.
claims.quote: So long as there is a flow of milk the menstrual purgations do not take place, at least as a general rule, though the discharge has been known to occur during the period of suckling.
measurable_quantities: duration of lactational amenorrhoea
proportion menstruating while breastfeeding
claims.candidate_data: Demographic and Health Surveys data on postpartum amenorrhoea and breastfeeding duration.

claims.label: Most animals show traces of the psychical qualities found in man
claims.claim: Most animals show traces of psychical qualities such as gentleness, fierceness, courage, timidity and something like sagacity, which differ from man's either in degree or by analogy.
claims.quote: In the great majority of animals there are traces of psychical qualities or attitudes, which qualities are more markedly differentiated in the case of human beings.
claims.candidate_data: Animal personality and comparative cognition studies bear on it, but the claim is framed conceptually; none known as a single dataset.

claims.label: Nature passes by degrees from lifeless things to animals with no sharp boundary
claims.claim: Nature proceeds little by little from lifeless things through plants to animals, so that no exact boundary can be drawn and intermediate forms cannot be assigned to one side or the other.
claims.quote: Nature proceeds little by little from things lifeless to animal life in such a way that it is impossible to determine the exact line of demarcation, nor on which side thereof an intermediate form should lie.
claims.scope: all living and non-living things; intermediate forms such as sponges, ascidians, sea-anemones and sessile shellfish
claims.candidate_data: none known

claims.label: More intelligent animals with memory stay longer with their young
claims.claim: Some animals simply breed at definite seasons, others also feed their young and then leave them, while the more intelligent animals with memory live with their offspring for longer and more socially.
claims.quote: other animals are more intelligent and endowed with memory, and they live with their offspring for a longer period and on a more social footing.
measurable_quantities: duration of parental care
relative brain size or cognitive measures
claims.candidate_data: Parental-care trait compilations with brain-size data, e.g. the Amniote Life-History Database combined with published mammal and bird brain-mass datasets.

claims.label: Air-breathing aquatic animals drown unless they surface to breathe
claims.claim: Some air-breathing animals that live in water, such as the sea-turtle, crocodile, hippopotamus, seal, freshwater tortoise and frog, choke or drown unless they breathe air from time to time, and they breed on or near land.
claims.quote: now all these animals choke or drown if they do not from time to time breathe atmospheric air: they breed and rear their young on dry land, or near the land, but they pass their lives in water.
claims.scope: sea-turtle, crocodile, hippopotamus, seal, freshwater tortoise, frog
measurable_quantities: obligate air breathing
breeding site (land or water)
claims.candidate_data: Life-history and respiration traits in AmphiBIO, the Animal Diversity Web and reptile trait compilations.

claims.label: The dolphin breathes air with lungs and suffocates when caught in nets
claims.claim: The dolphin breathes air into lungs, suffocates quickly when caught in nets, can live a considerable time out of water, and sleeps with its nose above water in order to breathe.
claims.quote: he also inhales air into his lungs; for, by the way, the creature is furnished with this organ and respires thereby, and accordingly, when caught in the nets, he is quickly suffocated for lack of air.
claims.scope: dolphins and other cetaceans with a blow-hole
measurable_quantities: presence of lungs
mortality from net entanglement
claims.candidate_data: Cetacean anatomy in Uberon/Phenoscape and bycatch mortality records in fisheries observer data.

claims.label: Aquatic animals take in water to cool the blood, as land animals take in air
claims.claim: Some aquatic animals take in water and discharge it for the same reason that air-breathers inhale air, to cool the blood; blooded animals that do this have gills, while those that take in water while catching prey have a blow-hole.
claims.quote: some aquatic animals take in water and discharge it again, for the same reason that leads air-breathing animals to inhale air: in other words, with the object of cooling the blood.
measurable_quantities: function of gill ventilation (gas exchange versus heat exchange)
claims.candidate_data: Comparative respiratory physiology literature on gill gas exchange and thermal exchange in fishes.

claims.label: The cordylus (water-newt) has gills instead of lungs yet walks on land
claims.claim: The cordylus or water-newt is the only known animal that takes in water through gills, having no lungs, yet is a four-footed animal that walks on land and gets its living there.
claims.quote: this creature is furnished not with lungs but with gills, but for all that it is a quadruped and fitted for walking on dry land.
claims.scope: cordylus (probably a larval or neotenic newt or salamander)
measurable_quantities: presence of gills and lungs in newt larvae and adults
terrestrial locomotion
claims.candidate_data: AmphiBIO and the Animal Diversity Web for respiration and life stages of European newts.

claims.label: A small change in a minute organ can change an animal's whole form
claims.claim: A change in a minute organ can cause an immense change in an animal's overall form; castration, mutilating one small organ, turns a male towards the female form, and a slight change in size of an essential organ in the embryo decides whether it becomes male or female.
claims.quote: The fact is that animals, if they be subjected to a modification in minute organs, are liable to immense modifications in their general configuration. This phenomenon may be observed in the case of gelded animals: only a minute organ of the animal is mutilated, and the creature passes from the male to the female form.
claims.scope: animals generally; castrated males; embryonic sex determination
measurable_quantities: morphological changes after castration
effect of early gonadal changes on sexual phenotype
claims.candidate_data: Endocrinology and developmental-biology literature on castration and gonadal sex determination.

claims.label: An empty wax vessel lowered into the sea fills with fresh water within a day
claims.claim: Sea water contains fresh water that can be strained from it: an empty thin vessel of moulded wax let down into the sea will within twenty-four hours contain fresh, drinkable water.
claims.quote: Take a thin vessel of moulded wax, attach a cord to it, and let it down quite empty into the sea: in twenty-four hours it will be found to contain a quantity of water, and the water will be fresh and drinkable.
claims.scope: sea water; sessile testaceans said to feed on fresh water
measurable_quantities: salinity of water collected in a sealed wax vessel after 24 hours submersion
claims.candidate_data: none known; would need a replication experiment.

claims.label: All fishes eat their own species except the mullet
claims.claim: All fishes eat members of their own species, with the single exception of the mullet; the conger is especially given to it.
claims.quote: All fishes devour their own species, with the single exception of the cestreus or mullet; and the conger is especially ravenous in this respect.
measurable_quantities: occurrence of cannibalism in diet studies by species
claims.candidate_data: Diet composition records in FishBase and published stomach-content studies.

claims.label: Fishes have the stomach next to the mouth and no gullet
claims.claim: Fishes have their stomachs close to the mouth and have no gullet, which is why some cast up their stomachs while chasing prey.
claims.quote: fishes have their stomachs close to the mouth, and are not furnished with a gullet.
measurable_quantities: presence and length of oesophagus in fishes
claims.candidate_data: Comparative fish anatomy in Uberon/Phenoscape (oesophagus annotations) and MorphoSource specimens.

claims.label: The parrot-fish is the only fish that chews the cud
claims.claim: Of all fishes the scarus (parrot-fish) is the only one known to chew the cud like a quadruped.
claims.quote: Of all fishes the so-called scarus, or parrot, wrasse, is the only one known to chew the cud like a quadruped.
claims.scope: Sparisoma cretense (Mediterranean parrotfish) versus other fishes
measurable_quantities: presence of regurgitation and re-chewing or pharyngeal grinding behaviour
claims.candidate_data: Feeding-behaviour and pharyngeal-jaw studies of parrotfishes; FishBase species accounts.

claims.label: Eels can live seven or eight years
claims.claim: The eel lives in some cases for seven or eight years.
claims.quote: The eel in some cases lives for seven or eight years.
measurable_quantities: eel lifespan
claims.candidate_data: Longevity records in AnAge and FishBase.

claims.label: Birds with crooked talons are all carnivorous and cannot swallow grain
claims.claim: Birds with crooked talons are carnivorous without exception and cannot swallow grain or bread even if it is put into their bills.
claims.quote: Of birds, such as have crooked talons are carnivorous without exception, and cannot swallow corn or bread-food even if it be put into their bills in tit-bits
claims.scope: raptors: eagles, kites, hawks, buzzard, lammergeier, vultures, owls
measurable_quantities: diet composition of raptors (proportion plant matter)
talon curvature
claims.candidate_data: EltonTraits diet data and AVONET morphology for birds of prey.

claims.label: Birds of prey almost never drink
claims.claim: Birds as a rule drink very little, and birds of prey never drink at all apart from a very few that drink very rarely, such as the kestrel and the kite.
claims.quote: In fact birds of prey never drink at all, excepting a very few, and these drink very rarely
measurable_quantities: drinking frequency in raptors
water intake from prey versus free water
claims.candidate_data: Avian water-balance physiology studies and field observations of raptor drinking.

claims.label: Oviparous animals have a spongy, bloodless lung and drink little
claims.claim: Scaly (tessellated) animals are spare drinkers, as are all animals with a spongy lung, and such a lung, poorly supplied with blood, is found in all oviparous animals.
claims.quote: Tessellated animals are spare drinkers, as are also all such animals as have a spongy lung, and such a lung, scantily supplied with blood, is found in all oviparous animals.
claims.scope: reptiles (lizards, snakes, tortoises) and other oviparous animals
measurable_quantities: lung structure and vascularization
water intake
claims.candidate_data: Comparative lung morphology literature and Uberon/Phenoscape annotations; reptile water-balance studies.

claims.label: Carnivores eat grass only when sick, to purge themselves
claims.claim: Fierce, jag-toothed viviparous quadrupeds are all carnivorous and never eat grass except when sick, as dogs eat grass to make themselves vomit.
claims.quote: These carnivorous animals never eat grass except when they are sick, just as dogs bring on a vomit by eating grass and thereby purge themselves.
measurable_quantities: frequency of grass-eating in healthy versus sick dogs
vomiting after grass-eating
claims.candidate_data: Veterinary surveys of plant-eating in dogs and cats.

claims.label: A pig's carcass weighs five-sixths of its live weight
claims.claim: A pig fattens faster for its size than any other animal, and after slaughter its flesh weighs five-sixths of its live weight, the hair, blood and the rest making up the other sixth.
claims.quote: If a pig be weighed when living, you may calculate that after death its flesh will weigh five-sixths of that weight, and the hair, the blood, and the rest will weigh the other sixth.
measurable_quantities: dressing percentage (carcass weight / live weight)
claims.candidate_data: Agricultural carcass-yield statistics for pigs (FAO and national livestock statistics).

claims.label: Camels live about thirty years and occasionally to a hundred
claims.claim: Camels live for about thirty years; some live much longer, and some have been known to reach a hundred.
claims.quote: Camels live for about thirty years; in some exceptional cases they live much longer, and instances have been known of their living to the age of a hundred.
measurable_quantities: typical and maximum camel lifespan
claims.candidate_data: Longevity records in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

claims.label: The bee is the only insect that always avoids rotten food
claims.claim: The bee is the only insect that invariably avoids anything rotten and touches no food without a sweet juice.
claims.quote: The bee is the only insect that invariably eschews whatever is rotten
claims.scope: honey bee compared with other insects
measurable_quantities: acceptance of decaying food by honey bees and other insects
claims.candidate_data: Honey bee foraging studies and insect feeding-guild records.

claims.label: Cranes migrate from Scythia to the marshes at the source of the Nile
claims.claim: Cranes migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile rises.
claims.quote: for these birds migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile has its source.
measurable_quantities: breeding and wintering ranges
migration routes
claims.candidate_data: GBIF occurrence data, Movebank tracking data and eBird for common crane migration.

claims.label: Migrants are fatter leaving cold for warm lands than on the return
claims.claim: All animals are fatter when migrating from cold to warm regions than when migrating from warm to cold; the quail is fatter when it leaves in autumn than when it arrives in spring.
claims.quote: All creatures are fatter in migrating from cold to heat than in migrating from heat to cold; thus the quail is fatter when he emigrates in autumn than when he arrives in spring.
claims.scope: migratory animals, especially the common quail
measurable_quantities: body mass or fat score of migrants in autumn versus spring
claims.candidate_data: Bird-ringing body-mass and fat-score records from European ringing schemes and stopover studies.

claims.label: Birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued and mimics
claims.claim: As a general rule all birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued and given to mimicry, as is the parrot.
claims.quote: As a general rule all birds with crooked talons are short-necked, flat-tongued, and disposed to mimicry.
claims.scope: birds with hooked claws, including parrots and owls
measurable_quantities: neck length
tongue shape
vocal or gestural mimicry
claims.candidate_data: AVONET morphology and published vocal-mimicry surveys across bird families.

claims.label: The trichia leaves the Black Sea up the Danube into the Adriatic
claims.claim: The trichia is caught entering but never leaving the Black Sea because it alone swims north into the Danube and, where the river divides, down into the Adriatic.
claims.quote: The way of accounting for this phenomenon is that this fish, and this one only, swims northwards into the Danube, and then at the point of its bifurcation swims down southwards into the Adriatic.
claims.scope: trichia (probably a sardine or shad) in the Black Sea, Danube and Adriatic
measurable_quantities: migration routes of clupeids between the Black Sea and Adriatic
hydrographic connection of the Danube to the Adriatic
claims.candidate_data: Hydrography of the Danube basin and clupeid distribution and migration records in FishBase and GBIF.

claims.label: Animals hide away against extreme heat as well as extreme cold
claims.claim: Animals go into concealment (dormancy) as a refuge against extreme heat as well as extreme cold; shellfish all do so, snails in winter and the purple murex and scallop in the hottest season.
claims.quote: animals go into concealment by way of refuge against extreme heat, as well as against extreme cold.
claims.scope: animals generally; land snails, purple murex, scallop
measurable_quantities: occurrence of hibernation and aestivation by species and season
claims.candidate_data: Published records of aestivation and hibernation in molluscs and other animals; AnAge notes on dormancy.

claims.label: Snakes and lizards hide for four months in winter and eat nothing
claims.claim: Scaly animals such as the serpent, lizard, gecko and river crocodile go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter and eat nothing during that time.
claims.quote: all of which go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter, and during that time eat nothing.
measurable_quantities: duration of winter dormancy
feeding during dormancy
claims.candidate_data: Reptile brumation studies and life-history compilations for Mediterranean snakes and lizards and the Nile crocodile.

claims.label: Many birds hide in winter rather than migrate, including swallows
claims.claim: Many birds do not migrate to warmer countries but hide where they are in winter; swallows have often been found in holes without feathers, and the kite, stork, turtle-dove, lark and others go into hiding.
claims.quote: A great number of birds also go into hiding; they do not all migrate, as is generally supposed, to warmer countries.
claims.scope: swallow, kite, stork, owzel, turtle-dove, lark, thrush, starling, owl
measurable_quantities: winter presence or absence and torpor in these species
claims.candidate_data: GBIF and eBird winter occurrence records, Movebank tracking of swallows and storks, and studies of avian torpor.

claims.label: The she-bear gives birth during winter concealment and emerges in spring
claims.claim: The she-bear gives birth while in winter concealment and stays hidden until she brings the cubs out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice; bears eat nothing while hidden.
claims.quote: The female brings forth her young at this time, and remains in concealment until it is time to bring the cubs out; and she brings them out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice.
measurable_quantities: timing of birth relative to denning
den emergence date
feeding during denning
claims.candidate_data: Brown bear denning and reproduction studies; AnAge and PanTHERIA for reproductive timing.

claims.label: Crustaceans moult not once but repeatedly
claims.claim: Crabs, crawfish and lobsters slough their shells, becoming soft all over, and they do so not once for all but over and over again.
claims.quote: These animals also do not cast their skins once and for all, but over and over again.
measurable_quantities: number of moults over lifetime
claims.candidate_data: Crustacean growth and moult studies; SeaLifeBase species accounts.

claims.label: Fishes have no pestilential diseases like those of man and livestock
claims.claim: No pestilential (epidemic) disease is known to attack fishes as such diseases attack man, horses and oxen, although individual fishes do appear to fall sick.
claims.quote: We know of no pestilential malady attacking fishes, such as those which attack man, and horses and oxen among the quadrupedal vivipara
measurable_quantities: occurrence of epizootic mass mortality in wild fish
claims.candidate_data: WOAH (World Organisation for Animal Health) aquatic animal disease reports and the literature on wild fish epizootics.

claims.label: The purple murex dies within a day of tasting fresh water
claims.claim: Shellfish generally benefit from rain, but the purple murex is an exception: placed near a river mouth, it dies within a day of tasting fresh water.
claims.quote: if it be placed on a shore near to where a river discharges, it will die within a day after tasting the fresh water.
measurable_quantities: survival time under low salinity
claims.candidate_data: Salinity-tolerance experiments on Mediterranean murex snails; SeaLifeBase habitat data.

claims.label: The pig is the only animal known to get measles
claims.claim: The pig is the only animal known to suffer from 'measles' (pimples in the flesh, seen especially under the tongue), and pigs never get it while still sucklings.
claims.quote: The pig is the only animal known to be subject to measles.
claims.scope: pigs; 'measles' corresponds to cysticercosis (Taenia solium cysts)
measurable_quantities: host range of cysticercosis
age at infection in pigs
claims.candidate_data: Parasite host records for Taenia solium and other cysticerci in veterinary parasitology literature and the NHM host-parasite database.

claims.label: Rabies passes to every animal bitten by a mad dog except man
claims.claim: Rabies drives dogs mad and is fatal to them, and any animal bitten by a rabid dog catches it and dies, with the exception of man.
claims.quote: ary animal whatever, excepting man, will take the disease if bitten by a dog so afflicted; the disease is fatal to the dog itself, and to any animal it may bite, man excepted.
measurable_quantities: transmission and fatality of rabies in humans versus other animals
claims.candidate_data: WHO rabies surveillance and WOAH WAHIS animal rabies data.

claims.label: The ass tolerates cold least and is absent from Scythia
claims.claim: Of all animals of its kind the ass is least able to endure extreme cold, which is why it is not found on the shores of the Black Sea or in Scythia.
claims.quote: Of all animals on its of its kind it is the least capable of enduring extreme cold, which circumstance will account for the fact that the animal is not found on the shores of the Euxine, nor in Scythia.
claims.scope: donkey compared with horse and mule
measurable_quantities: cold tolerance
historical distribution of donkeys in cold regions
claims.candidate_data: Livestock census data (FAOSTAT) for donkey distribution by climate and physiological studies of donkey cold tolerance.

claims.label: All insects die when smeared with oil
claims.claim: All insects without exception die if smeared with oil, and die faster if the head is smeared and they are laid in the sun.
claims.quote: All insects, without exception, die if they be smeared over with oil; and they die all the more rapidly if you smear their head with the oil and lay them out in the sun.
measurable_quantities: mortality after oil application
time to death by application site
claims.candidate_data: Entomological studies of horticultural and mineral oil toxicity to insects.

claims.label: The leopard is absent from Europe while lions live in part of Greece
claims.claim: Lions are more numerous in Libya and in the part of Europe between the Achelous and the Nessus rivers; the leopard is more abundant in Asia Minor and is not found in Europe at all.
claims.quote: lions are more numerous in Libya, and in that district of Europe that lies between the Achelous and the Nessus; the leopard is more abundant in Asia Minor, and is not found in Europe at all.
claims.scope: lion and leopard in the ancient Mediterranean
measurable_quantities: historical and archaeozoological occurrence of lions and leopards in Greece and Europe
claims.candidate_data: Archaeozoological records and fossil occurrences in the Paleobiology Database and GBIF.

claims.label: Different species breed together if similar in size and gestation length
claims.claim: In Libya animals of different species meet at watering places and pair, and such pairs often breed if they are nearly the same size and have gestation periods of the same length.
claims.quote: such pairs will often breed if they be nearly of the same size and have periods of gestation of the same length.
measurable_quantities: hybrid fertility versus body-size and gestation-length differences between parent species
claims.candidate_data: Mammalian hybrid compilations combined with body mass and gestation data from PanTHERIA and AnAge.

claims.label: Wolves and dogs interbreed, and the Laconian hound is a fox–dog cross
claims.claim: Animals of different kinds produce hybrids: in Cyrene the wolf and the bitch couple and breed, and the Laconian hound is a cross between the fox and the dog.
claims.quote: Elsewhere also bastard-animals are born to heterogeneous pairs; thus in Cyrene the wolf and the bitch will couple and breed; and the Laconian hound is a cross between the fox and the dog.
measurable_quantities: occurrence of wolf–dog and fox–dog hybrids
claims.candidate_data: Canid genomic hybridization studies and records of wolf–dog admixture; reports on claimed fox–dog hybrids.

claims.label: A scaly fish's age can be told from the size and hardness of its scales
claims.claim: The age of a scaly fish can be told from the size and hardness of its scales.
claims.quote: The age of a scaly fish may be told by the size and the hardness of its scales.
measurable_quantities: scale size and hardness versus known age
claims.candidate_data: Fisheries scale-ageing (scalimetry) validation studies.

claims.label: Females are less spirited than males, except in the bear and leopard
claims.claim: In all animals with separate sexes the female is less spirited (less courageous) than the male, except in the bear and the leopard, where the female is the more courageous.
claims.quote: In all cases, excepting those of the bear and leopard, the female is less spirited than the male; in regard to the two exceptional cases, the superiority in courage rests with the female.
claims.scope: animals with separate sexes, with the bear and leopard as exceptions
measurable_quantities: sex differences in aggression or boldness scores across species
sex differences in defensive aggression in bears and leopards
claims.candidate_data: Comparative behavioural literature on sex differences in aggression and boldness; field studies of maternal defensive aggression in bears and large cats.

claims.label: Animals sharing a locality or food are enemies
claims.claim: Animals that live in the same localities or feed on the same food are enemies, and when food runs short animals of the same kind fight one another.
claims.quote: There is enmity between such animals as dwell in the same localities or subsist on the food. If the means of subsistence run short, creatures of like kind will fight together.
claims.scope: animals in general, intra- and interspecific
measurable_quantities: rates of interspecific aggression versus dietary and habitat overlap
intraspecific aggression under food limitation
claims.candidate_data: Dietary overlap data from EltonTraits combined with published studies of interference competition and food-limitation experiments.

claims.label: With unlimited food, wild animals would be tame to man and each other
claims.claim: If there were no shortage of food, animals that are now wild or afraid of man would become tame towards man and peaceable towards one another, as fed animals in Egypt show.
claims.quote: One may go so far as to say that if there were no lack or stint of food, then those animals that are now afraid of man or are wild by nature would be tame and familiar with him, and in like manner with one another.
claims.scope: wild animals generally, including predators such as crocodiles
measurable_quantities: flight initiation distance and aggression of animals under supplemental feeding versus controls
claims.candidate_data: Studies of supplemental feeding and habituation effects on flight initiation distance and aggression in wildlife.

claims.label: Stag antler points increase yearly until about six years old
claims.claim: Stags grow no horns in their first year, unbranched spikes in their second, two-pointed antlers in the third and three-pointed in the fourth, increasing in complexity until about six years old, after which antlers no longer indicate age.
claims.quote: In the third year the antlers are bifurcate; in the fourth year they grow trifurcate; and so they go on increasing in complexity until the creature is six years old: after this they grow their horns without any specific differentiation, so that you cannot by observation of them tell the animal's age.
measurable_quantities: antler tine count by known age
age at which tine count plateaus
claims.candidate_data: Long-term individual-based red deer studies (e.g. the Isle of Rum study) with known-age antler measurements.

claims.label: Hinds swallow the afterbirth immediately after giving birth
claims.claim: After giving birth, the hind (female deer) at once swallows the afterbirth, catching it before it falls to the ground.
claims.quote: The hinds after parturition at once swallow the afterbirth, and it is impossible to secure it, for the hind catches it before it falls to the ground
measurable_quantities: proportion of deer births followed by placentophagy
claims.candidate_data: Published observations of parturition behaviour in red deer and other cervids; comparative reviews of placentophagy in mammals.

claims.label: Sick animals treat themselves, e.g. dogs eat grass to vomit
claims.claim: Many quadrupeds treat their own ailments: dogs, when ill, eat a kind of grass that makes them vomit.
claims.quote: Many other quadrupeds help themselves in clever ways. Wild goats in Crete are said, when wounded by arrows, to go in search of dittany, which is supposed to have the property of ejecting arrows in the body. Dogs, when they are ill, eat some kind of grass and produce vomiting.
claims.scope: quadrupeds, with dogs as the stated case
measurable_quantities: association between illness signs and grass eating in dogs
frequency of vomiting after grass eating
claims.candidate_data: Veterinary surveys of grass eating in domestic dogs and the zoopharmacognosy literature on animal self-medication.
